source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Fusarium wilt (ជម្ងឺស្រពោនបណ្តាលមកពីផ្សិត, Fusarium Wilt): in Cambodia this disease is commonly seen at the young corn stage, soon after planting, when the seedling suddenly shows wilting symptoms and eventually dies. This disease harms the crop by disrupting water uptake and transport in the plant, since it later attacks/blocks the vascular system that carries water. When examining the base of a wilted plant, one may find symptoms consistent with root rot present as well.

This disease can be carried by contaminated seed and spread further through irrigation water; it can spread from the roots up into the stem, weakening the corn's root system, causing rot near the roots and browning throughout the vascular tissue, and can spread into the field from plant residue left in the soil. If corn seed is planted in a field with poor drainage, or where compacted soil retains water, or where prior crop debris is left decomposing in the soil, the risk of this disease increases in the following season.

Control and prevention measures suggested:
- Do not sow diseased seed.
- Remove infected plants promptly.
- Before planting, treat seed with a fungicide such as Mancozeb at about a 2% concentration; once symptoms of the disease are seen in the field, this measure should be applied within the recommended window (about the first 3-4 days after symptoms appear).
